structured_output.summary: California Education Code §49501.5(a) has applied since the 2022-23 school year. It requires public schools to give every pupil who asks a free breakfast and a free lunch each school day, whatever the family's income or federal eligibility. The household's 9-year-old is of school age, so the household gets positive free school meal support even though its roughly $166k income puts it far above the federal 130% and 185% cutoffs. The engine set the meal tier to FREE under California's universal program and returned $1,130.96 a year. That positive amount matches both the law and the output definition ("whether PolicyEngine returns positive annual free school meal support"). The consensus answer of 0 applied only the federal income test and missed California's universal-meals mandate.
